title: Tentative detection of the glycine isomer glycolamide in a hot molecular core
question: Whether the glycine isomer glycolamide is present in the hot molecular core G358.93-0.03 MM1 and how its abundance compares to chemically related amides (formamide and acetamide) across environments.

data.sensitivity: ~20 uJy beam^-1 (continuum); ~0.5 K per 0.5 km s^-1 channel (line cube)

what.value: Spectroscopic catalogs and line lists from CDMS, JPL, and Lille Spectroscopic Database

evidence.quote: The spectroscopic entries used in this model were retrieved from three main databases: CDMS (cite: Mul01; Mul05), the Jet Propulsion Laboratory database (cite: Pic98), and the Lille Spectroscopic Database (cite: Mot25).

external_data.citation: CDMS (cite: Mul01; Mul05), JPL (cite: Pic98), Lille Spectroscopic Database (cite: Mot25)

evidence.quote: the NH$_{2}$CHO column density was derived from NH$_{2}$$^{13}$CHO, scaled by the ratio $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C = 28$\pm$5 (cite: 2023A&A...670A..98Y).

what.value: Amide abundances in G+0.693-0.027, Sgr B2(N2), and G31.41+0.41 for comparison

evidence.loc: Comparison with other sources and chemical models
evidence.quote: For reference, observational data were compiled for the molecular cloud G+0.693-0.027 (cite: 2023ApJ...953L..20R; 2023MNRAS.523.1448Z) and two hot molecular cores including Sgr B2(N2) (cite: 2020A&A...639A.135S; 2017A&A...601A..49B) and G31.41+0.41 (cite: 2021A&A...653A.129C).

external_data.citation: Rivilla et al. 2023 (cite: 2023ApJ...953L..20R); Zeng et al. 2023 (cite: 2023MNRAS.523.1448Z); Sanz-Novo et al. 2020 (cite: 2020A&A...639A.135S); Belloche et al. 2017 (cite: 2017A&A...601A..49B); Colzi et al. 2021 (cite: 2021A&A...653A.129C)

recipe.goal: Calibrate visibilities, perform continuum self-calibration, and image continuum and line cubes
recipe.method: Initial calibration with ALMA pipeline, iterative line-free channel selection starting from findcont (< 3 sigma), three rounds of phase self-calibration with MT-MFS imaging, UV continuum subtraction with uvcontsub, and multiscale imaging of line cubes.
key_parameters: MT-MFS with two Taylor terms; multiscale scales = 0, 5, 15, 50, 150 pixels (continuum) and 0, 5, 15, 50 pixels (line)

recipe.goal: Extract spectra from offset position and perform full-source and amide LTE spectral modeling
recipe.method: Extract spectra from slightly offset position to reduce Doppler blending; construct a full source LTE model of all detected species in GILDAS CLASS/Weeds; optimize T_ex and N_t for GA, FA, NH2 13CHO, and AA using CLASS/ADJUST with SciPy Powell algorithm.
key_parameters: V_LSR fixed to -16.5 km s^-1; source size theta fixed to deconvolved continuum size
Line widths fixed to 1.4 km s^-1 (GA), 2.8 km s^-1 (FA), 2.0 km s^-1 (NH2 13CHO), and 2.1 km s^-1 (AA)
assumptions: 12C/13C = 28 +/- 5 to scale NH2 13CHO to total NH2CHO column density
Conservative 20% uncertainty on T_ex and N_t

recipe.goal: Verify GA excitation temperature via rotational diagram analysis
recipe.method: Fit linear relation between ln(N_u/g_up) and E_up using integrated intensities of seven unblended GA transitions.
key_parameters: 7 unblended transitions of GA with E_u = 108 to 389 K
assumptions: LTE, optically thin emission, and beam-filling factor of unity

recipe.goal: Map spatial distribution of FA, AA, and GA
recipe.method: Generate integrated-intensity (moment 0) maps of verified unblended transitions using CARTA and compare with 1 mm continuum peak.

recipe.goal: Derive H2 column density from 1 mm dust continuum and compute relative molecular abundances and ratios
recipe.method: Calculate beam-averaged N(H2) from 1 mm dust continuum emission and compute fractional abundances chi = N_t / N(H2) and abundance ratios FA/AA, AA/GA, and FA/GA.
key_parameters: R_gd = 100; mu = 2.8; kappa_nu = 2 cm^2 g^-1 at ~1 mm; T_dust = 150 K
assumptions: Optically thin thermal dust emission, R_gd = 100, mu = 2.8, kappa_nu = 2 cm^2 g^-1, T_dust = 150 K, and 20% uncertainty on N(H2)

score_reason: Public archival ALMA data (2019.1.00768.S), supplementary line lists and full source model parameters hosted on Zenodo, and clear description of self-calibration, imaging, and LTE fitting steps; minor deductions for unstated spectral extraction coordinates, fixed source size value, and tclean pixel/threshold parameters, plus a typo in the abstract's GA abundance value.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA dataset with well-defined self-calibration and LTE spectral fitting workflow producing quantitative column densities, excitation temperatures, and abundance ratios.
